hypothesis: A task family whose members all factor through a shared latent Z admits Z as the coarsest common sufficient statistic; a family whose members reveal individual coordinates instead admits only the identity as a common sufficient statistic; and the family CSS is strictly finer than any single task's minimal sufficient statistic.

controls.description: The generative latent Z = joint(parity{0,1}, parity{2,3}) is explicitly in the enumerated quotient library, so the coarsest common sufficient statistic is representable.
A parallel task family that reveals individual bits (not shared through Z) makes the coarsest common sufficient statistic collapse to the identity, exhibiting the dissociation.
All 2^4 = 16 worlds and all quotients in the lattice are enumerated, so every entropy is exact and no sampling error appears.

gates.criterion: The coarsest common sufficient statistic of the shared family equals the latent Z (joint of the two disjoint pair-parities, image size 4).
The coarsest common sufficient statistic of the shared family has image size strictly less than 2^4 = 16.
The coarsest common sufficient statistic of the not-shared family is the identity map (image size 16).
The family CSS's image size for the shared family is strictly greater than the largest per-task minimal sufficient statistic image size.
